🇮🇳 India answer the T20I hammering — 6-wicket win over England at Edgbaston.

Axar Patel: 4/62 with the ball, unbeaten 57 with the bat, sealing the chase with Washington Sundar's 52* after Gill's 80 (retired hurt) laid the base.

England's 258 wasn't enough. POTM: Axar Patel. 🔥

tweet:
🖤 New Zealand hit back — 5-wicket win over West Indies at Providence.

West Indies were cruising at 63/0 before Jayden Lennox turned into an absolute menace, ripping out a career-best 5/19 to fold them for just 138. John Campbell's 43 was the only thing resembling resistance.

New Zealand's chase wasn't exactly serene either — 96/5 on a pitch spinning like a fairground ride — until Tom Latham (37*) and Mark Bracewell calmly walked them home.

New Zealand won by 5 wickets with 104 balls to spare. Player of the Match: Jayden Lennox. Series tied 1-1 — Providence giving nobody an easy day. 🔥
imageSource: ESPNcricinfo — Jayden Lennox celebrating during his career-best 5/19, West Indies vs New Zealand, 2nd ODI, Providence, 13 Jul 2026 (this match, NZ ODI kit, live action)

tweet:
🇮🇳 India didn't just win at Lord's — they redecorated the honours board.

285 all out, built on Mandhana (83), Harmanpreet (58) & Deepti Sharma (57). Debutant Kranti Gaud then turned the Long Room into a horror movie, ripping through England for 170.

Set an outrageous 457, Yastika Bhatia shrugged and became the first woman in history to score a Test century at Lord's (112) — then kissed the pitch for good measure. England folded for 186.

142 years Lord's waited to host a women's Test. India showed up and won it by 270 runs. New landlords at the Home of Cricket. 🔥
imageSource: France 24 (AFP) — Yastika Bhatia batting for India, England Women vs India Women, inaugural Women's Test, Lord's, 12 Jul 2026 (this match, India Test whites, live action)

tweet:
Bazball just lost a Test match it can't come back from. 🏴

McCullum's stepped down as England's Test coach — a 4-1 Ashes flogging and a 2-1 home series defeat to New Zealand did what four years of "just enjoy yourselves lads" couldn't survive.

The twist: he keeps the white-ball job, where England are No.1 in the world. Turns out the format with fewer vibes and more discipline is the one still standing.

Four years, one format left. 🔥
